questions.q: How does the summary describe the ego?
a: A room built from thoughts whose windows limit how we see
A wall that meditation must completely destroy
A voice that only appears during deep sleep
A gift that grows stronger the more you practice
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the room-and-windows image and says meditation lets you come and go.

questions.q: What does the summary recommend for people who get restless sitting still?
a: Try hatha yoga, t'ai chi, karate, singing or dancing first
Meditate only while lying in bed at night
Skip meditation and read spiritual books instead
Use a phone app that provides louder guidance
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the important thing is what the mind is doing, not the body.

questions.q: How long does the summary suggest committing to a new meditation practice?
a: At least two weeks
At least two months
Three days
One full year
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to commit for at least two weeks before judging whether it works.

questions.q: What should you do if meditation brings tingling, visions or ecstasy?
a: Acknowledge the experience and let it go
Chase it until it happens again
Tell your teacher you have finished
Stop meditating for several months
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns not to chase such experiences, only to notice and release them.

questions.q: What is spiritual pride in the summary?
a: Believing you are fully liberated when you can still grow
Refusing to meditate in a group setting
Feeling ashamed of your daily practice
Doubting every teacher you ever meet
questions.why: Lesson 3 says early progress can trick you into complacency.
